messages:
ana (support): Heads-up — customer ACME reported mixed-up tool results when using parallel tool calls. They say tool A's output sometimes appears as tool B's tool_result. Happening intermittently at ~500 RPS on their Dedicated pool. Request example and logs below.

ana (support): Customer: acme-inc, endpoint: POST /v1/run-tools, sdk: node v4.2. Payload:```json
{
  "prompt": "Summarize and classify:",
  "tools": ["summarizer", "labeler"],
  "mode": "parallel",
  "client_request_id": "acme-req-9876"
}
```

ana (support): They attached a response where tool_result ids map to wrong tool names. Example response snippet:```json
[{
  "tool": "summarizer",
  "result_id": "r_abc123",
  "output": "LABEL: urgent"
},
{
  "tool": "labeler",
  "result_id": "r_def456",
  "output": "Full summary text..."
}]
```

ana (support): They claim correlation_id header and x-request-id are present: x-request-id: rq-acme-202603. Raised P1 with customer, asking for triage. :grimacing:

dev-bot: New support ticket created: S-8342. Attached logs & customer repro.

mike (eng-runtime): @ana thanks. Can you paste the raw request/response stream (no redaction) and the routing correlation_id from the logs? Also which client SDK version and whether they used multi_tool_use.parallel wrapper?

ana (support): Full request attached to ticket S-8342. They used our multi_tool fanout (internal flag parallel=true). SDK: node-infer 1.9. Customer provided a short repro script they run at scale.

sarah (eng-infra): Quick thought — could be tool_result association relying on array index + async returns. If results are matched by position after concurrent completion, out-of-order completions could mis-align without a stable per-call identifier. Do we include a unique call_id per tool invocation in the runtime?

mike (eng-runtime): We include a per-request correlation id but I don't think individual tool calls were injected with unique call_ids in older parallel path. That could explain reuse if cache or worker reuses slot ids. Need to reproduce.

lee (customer-success): Customer is on Dedicated with high QPS and quantized workers. They're very unhappy because labels vs summaries swapped occasionally in prod. They've paused feature and want ETA for fix.

ken (oncall): Assigning to @mike for now. I'll stand by for rollover if needed.

mike (eng-runtime): Repro attempt steps I'm going to run: 1) spin up same dedicated pool config, 2) run their script at 500 RPS, 3) collect x-request-id traces + worker logs. If I can trigger, will attach heap/trace. Posting a quick curl-based repro so others can try:```bash
for i in {1..1000}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/run-tools -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-request-id: mq-$i" -d '{"prompt":"test","tools":["summarizer","labeler"],"mode":"parallel","client_request_id":"test-'$i'"}' &
 done; wait
```

mike (eng-runtime): If anyone else can repro in staging, add `?debug=fanout` to log per-tool call IDs.

ana (support): Customer provided one concrete example trace. Pasting simplified timeline:```
[2026-03-09T14:02:11Z] rq-acme-202603 recv request -> fanout to worker W1 & W2
[2026-03-09T14:02:11Z] W2 completes labeler -> returns result r_def456
[2026-03-09T14:02:11Z] W1 completes summarizer -> returns result r_abc123
[2026-03-09T14:02:11Z] Serve layer maps results: index 0->r_def456, index1->r_abc123 => swapped
```

sarah (eng-infra): That mapping behavior lines up with a positional reassembly bug. Wondering if batching optimization collapsed call order. Any chance the fanout uses a shared ring buffer index that's not cleared quickly?

mike (eng-runtime): Good catch. There's a fast-path that reuses a small pool of result slots and writes by slot id. If two calls complete close together, the aggregator might read slots by iteration rather than matching explicit tool call_id. I'll instrument slot write/read semantics.

opsbot: Incident created: INC-1127 (parallel tool result misassociation). Severity: P1. Notifying oncall.

ana (support): Customer asked for temporary mitigation — they'd accept forcing sequential tool calls even with perf hit. Any quick flag we can toggle for them?

mike (eng-runtime): Yes. We can flip the fanout mode to sequential per-request for that customer's pool: set header X-Redwood-Tool-Mode: sequential or set parallel=false on their config. That should avoid mis-association. I'll prepare change and coordinate with infra for a config push.

lee (customer-success): I'll ask customer to enable sequential mode and test. Not ideal but buys us time.

mike (eng-runtime): Root cause (prelim): result aggregator assumed tool order preserved by completion array. Fix plan: 1) require per-tool invocation UUID that travels with worker response, 2) aggregate by UUID rather than array index. Working on PR.

mike (eng-runtime): Draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/2448 (patch adds tool_call_id and guarded aggregator refactor). Marking for review.

sarah (eng-infra): We'll help validate in staging with the customer's repro. @mike please ping when PR is ready and we'll run scaled tests.

mike (eng-runtime): PR opened and tests added. Running staging run now.

opsbot: Update: INC-1127 state -> investigating.

ana (support): Customer switched to sequential mode and ran for 12h — no mismatches, they've resumed traffic but are cautious. Customer asked for ETA on permanent fix and revert plan.

mike (eng-runtime): If staging validation passes, aiming to roll patch to Dedicated fleets in 48 hours with canary to 5% then 50% then 100%. I'll post rollout plan here.

ken (oncall): I'll own the canary metrics watch and rollback plan. Add health checks: mismatch-rate metric + token correctness check.

lee (customer-success): Customer satisfied with workaround and timeline. Moving to status: acknowledged.

mike (eng-runtime): Final note: root cause was aggregator reliance on array position + slot reuse under high concurrency. Fix ensures stable tool_call_id in responses and aggregator matches by id. Follow-up: add e2e regression test using parallel fanout and randomized completion ordering.

ana (support): Closing loop with customer now. Adding postmortem to postmortems/ once incident is resolved. :white_check_mark:
